subject: general
question: The selling price of 25 books is equal to the cost price of 37 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: 25 × **Selling Price (SP)** = 37 × **Cost Price (CP)**.

Ratio of SP to CP: SP ÷ CP = 37 ÷ 25.

Profit = 37 − 25 = 12 units.

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (12 ÷ 25) × 100.

Profit% = 12 × 4 = 48%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → SP of 25 books = CP of 37 books.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86e55bfcc575af5b5f2346f5617ad2ce363a84fda46b48c4bbc5921363e96095.png] 
⇒ Let CP of 1 book be 1 unit.
⇒ CP of 25 books = 25 units.
⇒ SP of 25 books = CP of 37 books = 37 units.
⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 37 − 25 = 12.
⇒ Profit% = (12 ÷ 25) × 100 = 48%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When the CP of x articles equals the SP of y articles, the gain or loss depends on whether x is greater or less than y. Profit% = [(x − y) ÷ y] × 100.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss percentages are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise in the problem.</p
